1.description: Robins singing from bare branches and garden fences, defending winter territories
1.childFriendlyNote: A little bird with a bright orange chest sits on a fence and sings even in the cold. It's telling others this garden is mine!

1.description: Christmas roses blooming in sheltered garden borders, waxy white or pink flowers nodding in the cold
1.childFriendlyNote: These tough flowers bloom when everything else is sleeping. They don't mind the cold one bit!

1.description: Flocks of fieldfares from Scandinavia feeding on hedgerow berries and in open fields
1.childFriendlyNote: Big chattering groups of speckled birds gobble up berries. They flew here from the frozen north!

1.description: Grey herons standing motionless at canal edges and park ponds, hunting fish in winter
1.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey bird stands perfectly still by the water like a statue. Then snap! It catches a fish!

1.description: Magpies conspicuous in bare trees, their black and white plumage and long tails easy to spot
1.childFriendlyNote: Black and white birds with long tails strut around like they own the place. Their feathers flash blue and green in the light!

1.description: Velvet shank and jelly ear fungus growing on dead wood and elder branches in damp woodland
1.childFriendlyNote: Wobbly brown ears growing on branches. Jelly ear fungus feels just like a cold, rubbery ear!

2.description: Robins singing from bare branches and garden fences, defending winter territories
2.childFriendlyNote: A little bird with a bright orange chest sits on a fence and sings even in the cold. It's telling others this garden is mine!

2.description: Christmas roses blooming in sheltered garden borders, waxy white or pink flowers nodding in the cold
2.childFriendlyNote: These tough flowers bloom when everything else is sleeping. They don't mind the cold one bit!

2.description: Grey herons standing motionless at canal edges and park ponds, hunting fish in winter
2.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey bird stands perfectly still by the water like a statue. Then snap! It catches a fish!

2.description: Flocks of fieldfares from Scandinavia feeding on hedgerow berries and in open fields
2.childFriendlyNote: Big chattering groups of speckled birds gobble up berries. They flew here from the frozen north!

2.description: Green mistletoe balls clearly visible in bare tree canopies, white berries still clinging
2.childFriendlyNote: Green balls hang in the bare trees like bird nests. But they're actually a plant growing up in the sky!

3.description: Robins singing from bare branches and garden fences, defending winter territories
3.childFriendlyNote: A little bird with a bright orange chest sits on a fence and sings even in the cold. It's telling others this garden is mine!

3.description: Great tits starting to sing their two-note "tea-cher, tea-cher" song on milder days
3.childFriendlyNote: A bright yellow bird on a branch calls "tea-cher, tea-cher". Can you copy the tune?

3.description: Grey herons at canal edges and park ponds, some already returning to heronries
3.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey bird stands perfectly still by the water like a statue. Then snap! It catches a fish!

3.description: Flocks of fieldfares still feeding on remaining hedgerow berries
3.childFriendlyNote: Big chattering groups of speckled birds gobble up berries. They flew here from the frozen north!

3.description: Magpies conspicuous in bare trees, beginning to inspect old nests and potential nest sites
3.childFriendlyNote: Black and white birds with long tails strut around like they own the place. Their feathers flash blue and green in the light!

4.description: First snowdrop shoots pushing through cold soil, white drooping bells in sheltered garden corners and woodland edges
4.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white bells brave the cold like little lanterns poking out of the frozen ground, spring's first whisper!

4.description: Long yellow catkins beginning to dangle from bare hazel branches, releasing pollen on dry days
4.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow tails hang from branches like caterpillars. Shake one gently and watch golden dust fly!

4.description: Robins singing strongly, establishing territories ahead of the breeding season
4.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings louder now. It's getting ready for spring and wants everyone to hear!

4.description: Great tits singing their two-note "tea-cher, tea-cher" song from treetops, louder each week
4.childFriendlyNote: A bright yellow bird on a branch calls "tea-cher, tea-cher". Can you copy the tune?

4.description: Grey herons returning to heronries, large stick nests visible in tall trees near water
4.childFriendlyNote: The tall grey birds are building huge stick nests at the top of trees. Look for their messy twig platforms!

5.description: Snowdrops now in full bloom, carpets of white bells in parks, gardens and churchyards
5.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of tiny white bells nod in the breeze. Bend down close and sniff their sweet honey smell!

5.description: Hazel catkins fully extended, dangling yellow-gold and releasing clouds of pollen
5.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow tails hang from branches like caterpillars. Shake one gently and watch golden dust fly!

5.description: Great tits singing loudly from treetops, marking territory for the coming spring
5.childFriendlyNote: A bright yellow bird on a branch calls "tea-cher, tea-cher". Can you copy the tune?

5.description: First crocuses pushing through in parks and gardens, purple, yellow and white cups opening on sunny days
5.childFriendlyNote: Little cups of purple and gold pop open when the sun shines. They close up again at night like sleepy flowers!

5.description: Robins singing at dawn and dusk, pairs forming for breeding season
5.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings louder now. It's getting ready for spring and wants everyone to hear!

6.description: Snowdrops in full bloom, carpets of white bells in parks and woodland edges
6.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of tiny white bells nod in the breeze. Bend down close and sniff their sweet honey smell!

6.description: Hazel catkins fully extended and shedding pollen freely on dry days
6.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow tails hang from branches like caterpillars. Shake one gently and watch golden dust fly!

6.description: Crocuses blooming in parks, gardens and along canal paths, carpets of purple and gold
6.childFriendlyNote: Little cups of purple and gold pop open when the sun shines. They close up again at night like sleepy flowers!

6.description: Great tits singing loudly and persistently, one of the first birds to announce spring
6.childFriendlyNote: A bright yellow bird on a branch calls "tea-cher, tea-cher". Can you copy the tune?

6.description: Frogs migrating to ponds at night, listen for quiet croaking at dusk near water
6.childFriendlyNote: Frogs are waking up and hopping to ponds in the dark. They might cross paths and roads at night!

7.description: Snowdrops still blooming but beginning to fade in warmer spots
7.childFriendlyNote: The little white bells are starting to droop. They did their job waking up the garden!

7.description: Crocuses at their best in parks and gardens, masses of purple, yellow and white
7.childFriendlyNote: Little cups of purple and gold pop open when the sun shines. They close up again at night like sleepy flowers!

7.description: Frogs gathering in ponds, frogspawn appearing in sheltered shallows
7.childFriendlyNote: Blobs of see-through jelly with tiny black dots. Each dot is a baby frog! Watch them wriggle!

7.description: Great tits singing persistently, exploring nest boxes and tree holes
7.childFriendlyNote: A bright yellow bird on a branch calls "tea-cher, tea-cher". Can you copy the tune?

7.description: Daffodil shoots emerging, green spears poking through soil in parks and gardens
7.childFriendlyNote: Green swords push up through the mud. They're getting ready to burst into golden trumpets!

8.description: Crocuses fading in warmer spots but still blooming in cooler areas
8.childFriendlyNote: The colourful crocus cups are getting tired now. They've been partying since February!

8.description: Frogspawn swelling in pond shallows, jelly-like masses with black dots visible
8.childFriendlyNote: Blobs of see-through jelly with tiny black dots. Each dot is a baby frog! Watch them wriggle!

8.description: Early daffodils opening their yellow trumpets in parks and along canal banks
8.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow trumpets bob in the breeze. Spring is really coming now!

8.description: Glossy yellow star-shaped flowers appearing on banks and woodland edges
8.childFriendlyNote: Shiny yellow stars appear on the ground. Their petals glow like tiny suns!

8.description: Male blackbirds beginning to sing their rich fluting song from rooftops and treetops at dawn
8.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird with an orange beak sits on a rooftop and sings the most beautiful song at sunrise!

9.description: Daffodils in full bloom in parks, gardens and along roadsides
9.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow trumpets bob in the breeze. Spring is really here!

9.description: Celandine flowers spreading across woodland floors and stream banks
9.childFriendlyNote: The woodland floor twinkles with yellow stars. Each shiny petal catches the light!

9.description: Blackbirds singing their rich fluting song from rooftops and treetops at dawn and dusk
9.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird with an orange beak sits on a rooftop and sings the most beautiful song at sunrise!

9.description: Frogspawn developing, embryos visible wriggling inside the jelly
9.childFriendlyNote: The tiny black dots in the frog jelly are getting bigger. Look closely and you can see them wriggle!

9.description: Queen bumblebees emerging from hibernation, visiting early crocuses and willows for nectar
9.childFriendlyNote: A big fuzzy bee bumbles past. She's a queen who slept all winter and now she's very hungry!

9.description: Pale yellow primroses appearing on woodland banks and hedgerow bases
9.childFriendlyNote: Soft yellow flowers peek out from under hedges. Their name means "first rose" of spring!

10.description: Daffodils at their peak in parks, gardens and along canal paths
10.childFriendlyNote: Golden trumpets everywhere, whole fields of them nodding and bobbing in the wind!

10.description: Celandine flowers carpeting woodland floors and stream banks
10.childFriendlyNote: The woodland floor twinkles with yellow stars. Each shiny petal catches the light!

10.description: Blackbirds singing their rich fluting song from rooftops and treetops at dawn and dusk
10.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird with an orange beak sits on a rooftop and sings the most beautiful song at sunrise!

10.description: First brimstone butterflies emerging from hibernation, bright yellow males fluttering along hedgerows
10.childFriendlyNote: A butter-yellow butterfly flutters past. It slept all winter and now it's hungry for flowers!

10.description: Queen bumblebees actively visiting spring flowers, searching for nest sites in the ground
10.childFriendlyNote: A big fuzzy bee bumbles past. She's a queen looking for a cozy hole in the ground to build her nest!

10.description: Primroses blooming on woodland banks, hedgerow bases and in gardens
10.childFriendlyNote: Soft yellow flowers peek out from under hedges. Their name means "first rose" of spring!

11.description: Blackbirds in full song from rooftops, one of the richest dawn chorus voices
11.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird with an orange beak sits on a rooftop and sings the most beautiful song at sunrise!

11.description: Brimstone butterflies active on warm days, visiting primroses and violets for nectar
11.childFriendlyNote: A butter-yellow butterfly flutters past. It slept all winter and now it's hungry for flowers!

11.description: White storks returning from Africa, arriving at rooftop and chimney nests in the Netherlands and Germany
11.childFriendlyNote: Huge white birds with red legs land on rooftops and chimneys. They flew all the way from Africa to come home!

11.description: Primroses blooming strongly on woodland banks and hedgerow bases
11.childFriendlyNote: Soft yellow flowers peek out from under hedges. Their name means "first rose" of spring!

11.description: First wild cherry trees beginning to bloom, clouds of white and pale pink flowers on bare branches
11.childFriendlyNote: Whole trees burst into fluffy pink and white clouds. It looks like the tree is wearing a fancy party dress!

11.description: Tadpoles hatching from frogspawn, tiny black wrigglers in pond shallows
11.childFriendlyNote: The little black dots hatched! Tiny tadpoles wriggle through the water with their wiggly tails!

12.description: Wild cherry trees blooming, clouds of white and pale pink blossom in parks and along streets
12.childFriendlyNote: Whole trees burst into fluffy pink and white clouds. Petals float down like confetti!

12.description: Blackbirds in full song, one of the richest voices in the morning dawn chorus
12.childFriendlyNote: Wake up early and listen. The shiny black bird makes up a new song every morning!

12.description: White storks settling on nests, repairing their huge stick platforms on rooftops and chimneys
12.childFriendlyNote: The big white storks click their beaks together like castanets. That's how they say hello to each other!

12.description: Brimstone butterflies active on warm days, seeking nectar from spring flowers
12.childFriendlyNote: A butter-yellow butterfly flutters past. It slept all winter and now it's hungry for flowers!

12.description: Daffodils still blooming strongly, beginning to fade in the warmest spots
12.childFriendlyNote: The golden trumpets are still nodding in the parks, but some are starting to droop and rest!

13.description: Cherry blossom at peak, streets and parks lined with spectacular pink and white canopies
13.childFriendlyNote: Walk under the cherry trees and petals float down like pink snow. Try to catch one!

13.description: White storks incubating eggs on their large rooftop nests, both parents taking turns
13.childFriendlyNote: The big storks are sitting on eggs in their giant stick nests. Mum and dad take turns keeping the eggs warm!

13.description: Blackbirds in full song, beginning to build nests in hedges and garden shrubs
13.childFriendlyNote: The shiny black bird sings from the rooftop and then sneaks into a bush with a beak full of twigs!

13.description: Wild garlic leaves carpeting damp woodland floors, strong garlicky smell when crushed
13.childFriendlyNote: Walk through the woods and it smells like pizza! Crush a leaf gently and sniff. It's wild garlic!

13.description: First swallows arriving from Africa, swooping low over fields and water to catch insects
13.childFriendlyNote: The first swallows are back from Africa! Watch them zoom and swoop like little acrobats catching flies!

14.description: Cherry blossom fading, petals drifting like confetti along the famous Bonn cherry avenue and city parks
14.childFriendlyNote: The cherry petals are falling like pink snowflakes. The ground looks like a fairy carpet!

14.description: Wild garlic spreading across damp woodland floors, star-shaped white flowers beginning to open
14.childFriendlyNote: The woods smell like a kitchen! White star flowers and garlicky green leaves cover the ground!

14.description: Swallows arriving in numbers, swooping low over fields and water to catch insects
14.childFriendlyNote: More swallows arriving every day from Africa! Watch them zoom and swoop like little acrobats!

14.description: Bluebell shoots emerging in ancient woodlands across Belgium and the Netherlands
14.childFriendlyNote: Green shoots are pushing up through the leaves on the woodland floor. Soon they'll turn into a blue carpet!

14.description: Storks incubating eggs, visible standing tall on nest platforms on rooftops and pylons
14.childFriendlyNote: The big storks are sitting patiently on eggs. They click their beaks to say hello when their partner comes back!

14.description: Horse chestnut buds swelling and bursting, sticky brown buds opening to reveal bright green leaves
14.childFriendlyNote: The sticky brown buds on the chestnut tree are cracking open. Bright green leaves unfurl like tiny fans!

15.description: Bluebells opening in ancient woodlands, carpets of violet-blue flowers with sweet scent
15.childFriendlyNote: The whole woodland floor turns blue like a fairy kingdom. Bend down and smell the sweet perfume!

15.description: Wild garlic in full flower, white stars above glossy green leaves in damp woodland
15.childFriendlyNote: The woods smell like pizza! Hundreds of tiny white stars float above garlicky green leaves!

15.description: Swallows now widespread, swooping over fields and collecting mud for nests
15.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are here! They pick up tiny balls of mud to build their cup-shaped nests under roofs!

15.description: First nightingales arriving from Africa, singing their spectacular song from dense thickets at dusk
15.childFriendlyNote: Listen at bedtime. A hidden bird sings the most amazing song with trills and whistles in the dark!

15.description: Horse chestnut trees leafing out fast, large palmate leaves unfurling from sticky buds
15.childFriendlyNote: The chestnut leaves open up like big green hands waving at you from the tree!

15.description: Lily of the valley leaves emerging in shaded woodland, green shoots pushing up through leaf litter
15.childFriendlyNote: Pairs of green leaves unfurl from the forest floor. Tiny white bells will hang between them soon!

16.description: Bluebells at their peak in Belgian and Dutch woodlands, spectacular carpets of violet-blue
16.childFriendlyNote: The whole woodland floor turns blue like a fairy kingdom. It looks like the sky fell into the forest!

16.description: Nightingales singing powerfully from dense thickets, their rich song carrying far at dusk and through the night
16.childFriendlyNote: Listen at bedtime. A hidden bird sings the most amazing song you've ever heard, with trills and whistles in the dark!

16.description: Horse chestnut flower candles forming, tall upright clusters of white and pink flowers emerging
16.childFriendlyNote: The chestnut tree is growing white candles at the tip of every branch, like a birthday cake tree!

16.description: Swallows building mud cup nests under eaves, swooping over meadows catching insects
16.childFriendlyNote: Swallows zoom past your head catching flies. They can eat hundreds of bugs in one day!

16.description: Lily of the valley flower stems emerging between paired leaves, tiny white bells beginning to open
16.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white bells hang in a row like fairy lanterns. Sniff carefully, they smell like heaven!

17.description: Lily of the valley blooming in shaded woodland and gardens, intensely fragrant white bells
17.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white bells hang like fairy lanterns between two green leaves. Sniff carefully, they smell amazing!

17.description: Horse chestnut candles opening, magnificent white and pink flower spikes standing upright on branches
17.childFriendlyNote: The chestnut tree is covered in white candles. Each one is packed with hundreds of tiny flowers!

17.description: Nightingales in full song from thickets, their extraordinary repertoire filling warm evenings
17.childFriendlyNote: Listen at bedtime. A hidden bird sings the most amazing song with trills and whistles in the dark!

17.description: First cuckoos calling from woodland edges, the unmistakable two-note "cuck-oo" carrying far
17.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo! Cuck-oo!". This sneaky bird never builds its own nest, it puts its eggs in other birds' homes!

17.description: Hawthorn hedges turning green with fresh leaves, flower buds forming in clusters
17.childFriendlyNote: The prickly hedges are covered in tiny green leaves now. Clusters of flower buds are getting ready to pop!

17.description: Stork chicks hatching in rooftop nests, fluffy white heads visible above nest rim
17.childFriendlyNote: Tiny fluffy stork babies peek over the edge of the huge nest. Their parents bring them frogs and fish!

18.description: Lily of the valley at its peak. In France, bunches are given as gifts on May Day (May 1st) for good luck
18.childFriendlyNote: In France today everyone gives these sweet-smelling white bells to friends for good luck, happy May Day!

18.description: Horse chestnut in full candle, magnificent flower spikes in white and pink lining city avenues
18.childFriendlyNote: The chestnut tree candles are all lit up! Look how the white flowers have little pink and yellow spots!

18.description: Cuckoos calling frequently from woodland edges and hedgerows, females sneaking eggs into other nests
18.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo! Cuck-oo!". This sneaky bird lays its eggs in other birds' nests so they do all the babysitting!

18.description: Hawthorn beginning to bloom, dense clusters of white flowers with a musky scent
18.childFriendlyNote: The prickly hedges explode with tiny white flowers. Lean in and smell, it's sweet and a bit funky!

18.description: First cornflowers appearing in field margins and wildflower meadows, vivid blue blooms
18.childFriendlyNote: The brightest blue flowers you ever saw pop up at the edges of fields. They're called cornflowers!

19.description: Hawthorn in full bloom, hedgerows foaming with creamy-white blossom and musky scent
19.childFriendlyNote: The hedges look like they're covered in whipped cream, thousands of tiny white flowers all at once!

19.description: Cuckoos calling persistently, their two-note song echoing across fields and woodland edges
19.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo! Cuck-oo!". Can you hear the sneaky bird? Count how many times it calls!

19.description: Elder bushes beginning to bloom, flat-topped clusters of tiny cream flowers with sweet muscat scent
19.childFriendlyNote: Creamy flower plates appear on the elder bush. Sniff them and they smell like fizzy lemonade!

19.description: Stork chicks growing fast, visible standing in the nest and begging for food
19.childFriendlyNote: The baby storks are getting bigger! They stand up in the nest and wave their wings to beg for dinner!

19.description: Lily of the valley still blooming in shaded woodland, fragrance lingering in damp air
19.childFriendlyNote: The sweet little white bells are still hanging on. Enjoy their perfume while they last!

19.description: Cornflowers blooming in field margins and wildflower strips, vivid blue among the green
19.childFriendlyNote: Electric blue flowers dot the meadow. They're the brightest blue in nature!

20.description: Hawthorn blossom at its peak, hedgerows white and fragrant
20.childFriendlyNote: The hedges look like they're covered in whipped cream, thousands of tiny white flowers everywhere!

20.description: Elder flowers opening everywhere, flat cream flower heads with intoxicating sweet scent
20.childFriendlyNote: Creamy flower plates appear on the elder bush. Sniff them and they smell like fizzy lemonade!

20.description: Linden trees fully leafed out, heart-shaped leaves creating deep shade along city boulevards
20.childFriendlyNote: The lime trees along the streets have heart-shaped leaves. Each one is a little love letter from the tree!

20.description: Cuckoos still calling, their foster chicks growing in other birds' nests
20.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo! Cuck-oo!". Somewhere a tiny warbler is feeding a cuckoo chick three times its size!

20.description: First red poppies appearing in field margins and disturbed ground, delicate scarlet petals
20.childFriendlyNote: Bright red poppies pop up at the edge of fields. Their petals are as thin as tissue paper!

21.description: Elder flowers at their peak, hedgerows and woodland edges dotted with cream flower plates
21.childFriendlyNote: Creamy flower plates are everywhere. People pick them to make elderflower cordial and pancakes!

21.description: Red poppies spreading in field margins and along roadsides, fields turning scarlet
21.childFriendlyNote: Bright red poppies dot the fields like splashes of paint. Their petals are as thin as tissue paper!

21.description: Linden trees in full leaf, creating tunnels of shade along European boulevards
21.childFriendlyNote: Walk under the lime trees and feel the cool shade. Look up and see thousands of heart-shaped leaves!

21.description: Cornflowers at their best in field margins, the national flower of France glowing vivid blue
21.childFriendlyNote: Electric blue flowers dot the meadow. They're France's favourite flower!

21.description: Swifts screaming through city skies in groups, dark scythe-shaped silhouettes circling above rooftops
21.childFriendlyNote: Listen for the screaming birds racing above the rooftops. Swifts eat, sleep and even drink while flying!

22.description: Elder flowers still blooming, beginning to fade and turn cream-brown at edges
22.childFriendlyNote: The elder flowers are starting to turn brown. Last chance to smell their fizzy lemonade scent!

22.description: Red poppies at their peak, fields and roadsides ablaze with scarlet
22.childFriendlyNote: Whole fields are painted red with poppies. Watch the petals flutter like butterfly wings in the breeze!

22.description: Swifts screaming through evening skies, nesting under eaves and in crevices
22.childFriendlyNote: Listen for the screaming birds racing above the rooftops. They never stop flying, even when they sleep!

22.description: Wild roses blooming in hedgerows, delicate pink and white five-petalled flowers
22.childFriendlyNote: Pink and white wild roses pop open in the hedges. They smell sweet but watch out for the thorns!

22.description: Linden flower buds forming, clusters of pale yellow buds hanging from leaf-like bracts
22.childFriendlyNote: Little yellow buds are hanging from the lime tree leaves. They're about to fill the whole city with sweet smell!

23.description: Dog roses in full bloom along hedgerows and woodland edges, delicate pink and white flowers
23.childFriendlyNote: Pink and white wild roses fill the hedges with sweet perfume. Each flower has just five petals!

23.description: Red poppies still blazing in field margins, seed pods beginning to form on oldest flowers
23.childFriendlyNote: Bright red poppies still paint the fields. Shake a dry seed head and hear the seeds rattle like a maraca!

23.description: Swifts screaming in groups above rooftops, feeding chicks tucked in roof crevices
23.childFriendlyNote: Screaming swifts race above the rooftops in groups. They're catching flies to feed their babies under the roof tiles!

23.description: Wildflower meadows at their best: ox-eye daisies, buttercups, clover and yarrow in full bloom
23.childFriendlyNote: The meadow is like a paint palette: white daisies, yellow buttercups, purple clover all mixed together!

23.description: Linden trees beginning to bloom, sweet honey scent drifting through city streets and boulevards
23.childFriendlyNote: The lime trees are starting to bloom and the whole street smells like honey. Listen to the bees buzzing in the branches!

24.description: Linden trees in full bloom, their sweet honey-like fragrance filling city boulevards and parks, humming with bees
24.childFriendlyNote: The whole city smells like honey! Lime trees buzz with thousands of bees collecting the sweetest nectar!

24.description: Dog roses in full bloom, hedgerows decorated with pink and white single flowers
24.childFriendlyNote: Pink and white wild roses fill the hedges. Each flower has just five delicate petals!

24.description: Swifts in full breeding mode, screaming parties racing low over rooftops in the warm evenings
24.childFriendlyNote: On warm evenings the swifts go crazy, screaming and chasing each other around the buildings at top speed!

24.description: Wildflower meadows at peak bloom: ox-eye daisies, buttercups, campion and scabious in full flower
24.childFriendlyNote: The meadow is bursting with flowers. Hold a buttercup under your chin and see if it glows yellow!

24.description: Dragonflies patrolling ponds and streams, broad blue-bodied males hovering over water
24.childFriendlyNote: A blue dragonfly hovers over the pond like a tiny helicopter. Its wings buzz so fast you can barely see them!

25.description: Linden trees at peak bloom, the signature summer scent of Western European cities, bees everywhere
25.childFriendlyNote: The whole city smells like honey! Stand under a lime tree and listen to the buzzing above you!

25.description: Dog roses beginning to fade, first petals falling, small green rose hips forming
25.childFriendlyNote: The wild rose petals are falling, but look! Little green balls are growing where the flowers were!

25.description: Summer wildflower meadows at peak: knapweed, yarrow, wild carrot and scabious humming with insects
25.childFriendlyNote: The meadow buzzes with bees and butterflies visiting every flower. It's like a busy insect restaurant!

25.description: Emperor dragonflies patrolling ponds and canals, large blue-green bodies glinting in sunlight
25.childFriendlyNote: A huge blue-green dragonfly zooms over the water like a tiny fighter jet. It catches other bugs mid-air!

25.description: Stork chicks growing large, practising wing-flapping on the nest while parents hunt in meadows
25.childFriendlyNote: The young storks stand on the nest flapping their wings. They're practising for their first flight!

26.description: Linden bloom fading, sticky honeydew dripping from aphid-colonized leaves, last waves of sweet scent
26.childFriendlyNote: The honey smell is fading. If you park under a lime tree your car gets sticky drops on it!

26.description: Lavender blooming in gardens, parks and in vast fields in southern France, buzzing with bees
26.childFriendlyNote: Purple lavender buzzes with bees. Rub a flower between your fingers and smell the lovely scent!

26.description: Dragonflies and damselflies abundant at ponds, canals and slow rivers
26.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom and hover over the water like tiny helicopters. They were here before the dinosaurs!

26.description: Young storks nearly full-grown, practising flights from the nest and landing nearby
26.childFriendlyNote: The young storks take their first wobbly flights from the nest. They look a bit clumsy at first!

26.description: Swifts still screaming over rooftops, feeding growing chicks in roof crevices
26.childFriendlyNote: The screaming swifts are still racing around. Their babies are getting big and hungry up in the roof!

27.description: Lavender at its peak in gardens and southern French fields, rich purple spikes buzzing with pollinators
27.childFriendlyNote: Purple lavender spikes are humming with bees. Rub a flower between your fingers and smell summer!

27.description: Dragonflies and damselflies abundant, hawking insects over ponds and waterways
27.childFriendlyNote: Big dragonflies zoom and hover over the water. Their wings shimmer like stained glass in the sun!

27.description: Late poppies still blooming in field margins, pepper-pot seed heads forming on older plants
27.childFriendlyNote: Some poppies are still red but others have turned into little pepper pots. Shake one and seeds sprinkle out!

27.description: Swifts still active over cities, young birds about to fledge from roof nests
27.childFriendlyNote: Young swifts are about to leave their nests for the very first time. Once they jump, they won't land again for years!

27.description: Elder berries forming, clusters of small green berries hanging where the flowers were
27.childFriendlyNote: Where the creamy flowers were, tiny green berries are now hanging in bunches. They'll turn dark purple!

28.description: Lavender still blooming strongly in gardens and parks, butterflies visiting frequently
28.childFriendlyNote: Purple lavender is still full of butterflies. Watch them unroll their long tongues to drink the nectar!

28.description: Swifts beginning to gather in screaming groups, young birds fledging, preparing for southward departure
28.childFriendlyNote: The swifts are getting ready to leave. Soon they'll fly all the way to Africa without stopping!

28.description: Sunflower fields beginning to bloom in France and Germany, massive yellow heads turning to face the sun
28.childFriendlyNote: Giant yellow flowers as big as dinner plates all face the same way. They follow the sun across the sky!

28.description: Dragonflies abundant at ponds and waterways, hawking insects in warm afternoon air
28.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom and hover over the pond. Can you spot the difference between big dragonflies and tiny damselflies?

28.description: Young storks fully fledged, families feeding together in meadows before autumn migration
28.childFriendlyNote: The stork families walk through meadows together catching frogs. Soon they'll fly all the way to Africa!

29.description: Sunflower fields in full bloom across France and Germany, spectacular seas of golden yellow
29.childFriendlyNote: Fields of giant sunflowers stretch as far as you can see. Each one is as big as your head!

29.description: Lavender fading in some gardens, still blooming in cooler areas and at higher elevations
29.childFriendlyNote: The lavender is starting to dry. Pick a sprig and keep it in your room for lovely sleepy-time smell!

29.description: Common darter dragonflies appearing, reddish males perching on sunny fence posts and twigs near water
29.childFriendlyNote: A little red dragonfly lands on a stick near the pond. It suns itself, then zooms off to catch a fly!

29.description: Elder berries ripening, clusters turning from green to deep purple-black
29.childFriendlyNote: The tiny berries are turning dark purple in big droopy bunches. Birds love eating them!

29.description: Swallows feeding second broods, young birds from first brood perching on wires in groups
29.childFriendlyNote: Young swallows line up on telephone wires like beads on a necklace. Their parents bring them snacks!

30.description: Sunflower fields at their peak, vast golden seas across the French and German countryside
30.childFriendlyNote: Miles and miles of sunflower faces all looking at the sun together. It's like a giant happy crowd!

30.description: Elder berries ripe and heavy, clusters of deep purple-black berries drooping on stems
30.childFriendlyNote: The elderberries are ripe. Dark purple bunches hang down and the birds are having a feast!

30.description: Common darter dragonflies active at ponds and in gardens, resting on warm surfaces
30.childFriendlyNote: Red dragonflies sun themselves on warm paths. They dart away and come right back to the same spot!

30.description: Swallows feeding growing second broods, swooping low over fields in the warm evening air
30.childFriendlyNote: Swallows swoop low over the grass catching flies. Watch how they twist and turn without crashing!

30.description: Garden spiders growing, webs becoming visible in morning dew across hedgerows and garden fences
30.childFriendlyNote: Spider webs sparkle with dewdrops in the morning sun. Each one is a tiny work of art!

31.description: Sunflowers beginning to droop and set seed, heads heavy with ripening seeds
31.childFriendlyNote: The sunflowers are nodding their heavy heads. They're filling up with seeds that birds and people love to eat!

31.description: Elder berries fully ripe, birds feeding heavily on the dark purple clusters
31.childFriendlyNote: Birds gobble the dark purple elderberries. Look for purple splats on the ground underneath!

31.description: Garden spiders' orb webs growing larger, glistening with morning dew in hedgerows and gardens
31.childFriendlyNote: The garden spiders are getting bigger. Each one sits in the middle of a beautiful circular web!

31.description: Early apples ripening on trees, first windfalls appearing on the ground in orchards and gardens
31.childFriendlyNote: The first apples are ready! Find a windfall on the ground. Does it smell sweet or sour?

31.description: Swallows gathering on wires in larger groups, beginning to prepare for autumn migration
31.childFriendlyNote: More and more swallows sit on the wires together. They're making plans for their big trip to Africa!

32.description: Apple harvest beginning, trees laden with fruit in orchards and gardens across the region
32.childFriendlyNote: Apple trees are loaded with fruit. Pick one, give it a polish on your shirt and take a crunchy bite!

32.description: Garden spiders at full size, large orb webs spectacular with morning dew
32.childFriendlyNote: Big garden spiders sit in sparkling dewy webs. Look for the white cross pattern on their round tummies!

32.description: Swallows gathering in large flocks on wires, feeding up for the long migration south
32.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of swallows line up on wires like musical notes. Soon they'll fly away to Africa!

32.description: Elder berries fully ripe, heavy purple-black clusters drooping from branches
32.childFriendlyNote: The last elderberries hang in heavy purple bunches. Blackbirds and starlings gobble them up!

32.description: Fire salamanders emerging after summer rain in woodland, striking black bodies with yellow spots or stripes
32.childFriendlyNote: After rain, look in the woods for a shiny black creature with bright yellow spots. It looks like it was painted!

33.description: Apple harvest in full swing, orchards busy and windfalls abundant on the ground
33.childFriendlyNote: Apple trees are loaded. Pick one up and smell it, each variety has its own special scent!

33.description: Fire salamanders active in damp woodland after rain, easily spotted with their yellow and black warning colours
33.childFriendlyNote: After rain, look carefully on the forest floor. A shiny black and yellow creature might be crawling by!

33.description: Garden spider webs everywhere, heavy with morning dew and catching late summer insects
33.childFriendlyNote: Every hedge and fence has a spider web strung across it. In the morning dew they look like diamond necklaces!

33.description: Swallows massing on wires and in reed beds, departure for Africa imminent
33.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are getting restless. Big groups chatter on the wires, planning their long journey south!

33.description: Pears ripening on trees in orchards and gardens, Williams and Conference varieties ready to pick
33.childFriendlyNote: The pears are ripe and juicy. Squeeze one gently to see if it's ready, then enjoy the sweet taste!

34.description: Main apple harvest continuing, later varieties colouring up beautifully on the tree
34.childFriendlyNote: Red, green and golden apples hang from the branches. It's harvest time!

34.description: Fire salamanders still active in woodland after rain, crossing paths and trails at night
34.childFriendlyNote: After rain, shine a torch on the forest path. You might spot a shiny black and yellow salamander!

34.description: Garden spiders at their largest, fat with eggs, webs strung across paths and between fence posts
34.childFriendlyNote: The garden spiders are huge now. Watch one repair its web, it's like watching a tiny artist at work!

34.description: First autumn mushrooms appearing after rain: field mushrooms, parasols and early boletes in grassland and woodland
34.childFriendlyNote: After rain, mushrooms pop up overnight like magic. Some are tiny buttons, some are big dinner plates!

34.description: Horse chestnut leaves beginning to turn brown and curl at edges, conker cases still green
34.childFriendlyNote: The chestnut leaves are going brown and crinkly. Look up and you'll see spiky green balls hiding the conkers inside!

35.description: Horse chestnut conkers ripening in their spiky green cases, first ones starting to split and fall
35.childFriendlyNote: The spiky green balls are starting to crack open: inside each one is a shiny brown conker treasure!

35.description: Late apple varieties ripening, orchards fragrant with fallen fruit
35.childFriendlyNote: The orchard smells amazing, sweet apples everywhere, on the tree and on the ground!

35.description: Mushroom season building: ceps, chanterelles and various boletes appearing in woodland after rain
35.childFriendlyNote: The mushroom hunt is on! Funny shapes pop up everywhere after rain. Some look like umbrellas, some like balls!

35.description: Last swallows departing, small groups still heading south, wires emptying day by day
35.childFriendlyNote: Wave goodbye to the last swallows. They're heading to Africa for winter and will be back in spring!

35.description: Garden spiders laying eggs in silk sacs, webs still catching morning dew beautifully
35.childFriendlyNote: The big garden spiders are wrapping up tiny silk parcels of eggs. Hundreds of baby spiders will hatch in spring!

36.description: Conkers falling from trees, spiky cases splitting open on impact to reveal shiny mahogany-brown nuts
36.childFriendlyNote: Conker season! Crack open the spiky green cases and find the glossy brown treasures inside. Who can find the biggest?

36.description: Cep mushrooms appearing under beech and oak trees, prized by foragers across Western Europe
36.childFriendlyNote: Fat brown mushrooms with spongy undersides hide under oak trees. People in France and Germany love eating these!

36.description: Late apple varieties at their best, fruit fragrant and colourful on the tree
36.childFriendlyNote: The last apples of the year are the sweetest. Enjoy them before winter comes!

36.description: Beech leaves just beginning to turn at the edges, first hints of golden-copper autumn colour
36.childFriendlyNote: The beech leaves are just starting to change. Green is turning to gold at the edges like autumn is painting them!

36.description: Starling flocks growing larger as autumn migrants arrive, roosting in urban trees and reed beds
36.childFriendlyNote: Shiny speckled birds are gathering in bigger and bigger groups. Soon they'll make amazing sky dances!

37.description: Conkers falling freely, leaves yellowing and browning, first autumn colour on chestnut avenues
37.childFriendlyNote: Conkers rain down from the trees. Collect the shiniest ones and feel how smooth they are!

37.description: Cep mushrooms still appearing after rain, chanterelles and other edible fungi in mixed woodland
37.childFriendlyNote: Mushroom treasure hunt! After rain, the forest floor is dotted with all kinds of weird and wonderful fungi!

37.description: Beech trees turning copper and gold, one of the most spectacular autumn colour trees in Europe
37.childFriendlyNote: The beech trees are turning the colour of a shiny new penny. Copper and gold leaves glow in the sun!

37.description: Starling flocks building, pre-roost aerial displays beginning over cities and reed beds
37.childFriendlyNote: Watch the starlings gather at sunset. They swirl around in the sky like a magic cloud that changes shape!

37.description: Red squirrels busy caching hazelnuts and acorns, burying them in the ground for winter stores
37.childFriendlyNote: Bushy-tailed red squirrels dash around burying nuts. They're hiding snacks for winter but sometimes forget where!

38.description: Beech trees in spectacular autumn colour, copper and gold canopies glowing in the sunlight
38.childFriendlyNote: Walk through a beech wood and everything glows copper and gold. It's like being inside a treasure chest!

38.description: Red squirrels frantically gathering and burying acorns, hazelnuts and beech mast for winter
38.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are in a hurry, digging, burying, digging, burying! Winter is coming and they need snacks!

38.description: Fly agaric toadstools appearing under birch trees, bright red caps with white spots. Do not touch
38.childFriendlyNote: The fairy-tale toadstool! Red with white spots. It looks magical but don't touch, it's poisonous!

38.description: Horse chestnut leaves browning and falling, last conkers dropping, trees looking ragged
38.childFriendlyNote: The chestnut trees are losing their big hand-shaped leaves. Crunch through the piles on the ground!

38.description: Starling murmurations growing spectacular, thousands of birds swirling above roost sites at dusk
38.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of starlings make amazing swirling shapes in the sky at sunset. It's nature's best dance show!

39.description: Beech trees in full autumn glory, copper leaves beginning to fall, beech mast crunching underfoot
39.childFriendlyNote: Crunch through the beech leaves and tiny spiky nutshells. Pick one up and find the little triangular nut inside!

39.description: Red squirrels still busily caching food, tufted ears becoming more prominent as winter coat grows in
39.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are getting fluffier. Their ear tufts are growing longer for winter!

39.description: Starling murmurations at their most spectacular, vast swirling clouds of birds at dusk
39.childFriendlyNote: The starling sky-dance is amazing. Thousands of birds swirl and twist like a living cloud at sunset!

39.description: First fieldfares arriving from Scandinavia, flocks appearing in hedgerows and open fields
39.childFriendlyNote: Chattering groups of speckled birds arrive from the frozen north. They flew here to eat our berries!

39.description: Fly agaric toadstools still appearing under birch trees, joined by puffballs and shaggy ink caps
39.childFriendlyNote: Stomp on a puffball mushroom and watch a brown dust cloud puff out. Those are millions of tiny spores!

40.description: Beech leaves falling in earnest, carpeting woodland floors in copper and rust
40.childFriendlyNote: Kick through the crunchy beech leaves. They're the colour of a fox's fur!

40.description: Starling murmurations continuing at dusk, massive flocks wheeling over city rooftops
40.childFriendlyNote: The starling sky-dance at sunset is nature's best show. No two evenings are the same!

40.description: Fieldfares arriving in larger flocks, stripping berries from hedgerows and rowan trees
40.childFriendlyNote: Noisy groups of fieldfares gobble up bright red berries. They flew from Scandinavia to feast!

40.description: Red squirrels making final food caches, thick winter coat now fully grown with prominent ear tufts
40.childFriendlyNote: The fluffy red squirrel has its thick winter coat on. Look at those amazing ear tufts like tiny paint brushes!

40.description: Oak trees turning bronze and yellow, acorns falling and being collected by jays and squirrels
40.childFriendlyNote: Acorns are falling like rain! Each tiny acorn could grow into a giant oak tree. Put one in your pocket for luck!

41.description: Oak trees in full autumn colour, bronze and golden-brown leaves, last acorns dropping
41.childFriendlyNote: The mighty oak tree is dressed in gold and brown. Collect an acorn in its cute little cup hat!

41.description: Fieldfares feeding actively in flocks, moving through hedgerows stripping berries
41.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares are working their way through the hedges. They chatter loudly while gobbling berries!

41.description: Starling murmurations at peak size, tens of thousands swirling above roost sites before dropping in
41.childFriendlyNote: The starling murmurations are huge now. The whole sky ripples and swirls like it's alive!

41.description: Peak autumn leaf fall: maple, beech, chestnut and oak leaves carpeting parks and streets in reds, golds and browns
41.childFriendlyNote: Crunch through piles of colourful leaves. Collect the prettiest reds, yellows and oranges for a leaf rainbow!

41.description: Holly berries ripening to bright red, glossy green leaves standing out as other trees go bare
41.childFriendlyNote: Bright red berries and shiny prickly leaves. The holly tree stays green when everything else goes bare!

42.description: Heavy leaf fall continuing, wet leaves piling up on paths and streets, rich earthy autumn smell
42.childFriendlyNote: Shuffle through the leaves and breathe in that special autumn smell, earthy and sweet and a bit mushroomy!

42.description: Starling murmurations continuing, dramatic shapes at dusk over cities and bridges
42.childFriendlyNote: The starlings make shapes in the sky. Sometimes it looks like a whale, sometimes a giant hand!

42.description: Fieldfares in full force, large flocks in hedgerows and on playing fields searching for invertebrates
42.childFriendlyNote: Groups of chattering fieldfares hop across the playing field. They're hunting for worms and bugs!

42.description: Holly berries bright red, the evergreen leaves vivid against bare deciduous branches
42.childFriendlyNote: The holly tree is showing off, shiny green leaves and bright red berries while everything else is bare!

42.description: Tawny owls calling in the dusk, the classic "twit-twoo" actually a duet between male and female
42.childFriendlyNote: "Twit-twoo!" That's actually two owls talking: one says "twit" and the other answers "twoo"!

43.description: Trees nearly bare, thick carpets of wet leaves on the ground, last holdouts clinging to oaks
43.childFriendlyNote: The trees are almost bare, but look at the thick crunchy carpet they've made on the ground!

43.description: Starling murmurations still spectacular, birds gathering before dropping into dense roosts
43.childFriendlyNote: The starling show goes on, wrap up warm and watch them swirl like a living painting in the sky!

43.description: Tawny owls calling regularly at dusk and before dawn, territorial hooting carrying through bare trees
43.childFriendlyNote: Listen when it's getting dark, "hoo-hoo-hooooo". The tawny owl is telling everyone this is its woodland!

43.description: Holly berries bright red against dark glossy leaves, one of the few splashes of colour in bare hedgerows
43.childFriendlyNote: Holly berries glow red like tiny traffic lights in the bare hedge. Birds love eating them!

43.description: Fieldfares continuing to work through berry crops, moving from hedge to hedge in noisy flocks
43.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares are still feasting. They chack-chack-chack as they fly from hedge to hedge!

44.description: Mistletoe becoming visible as host trees lose their leaves, green balls hanging in bare canopies
44.childFriendlyNote: Now the trees are bare you can spot the mistletoe, green balls hanging in the branches like bird nests!

44.description: Tawny owls calling in the lengthening darkness, hooting from churchyards and parks
44.childFriendlyNote: "Hoo-hoo-hooooo". The owl sings from the dark trees, it can see a mouse moving in pitch darkness!

44.description: Holly berries at their brightest, a vital food source for thrushes and other berry-eating birds
44.childFriendlyNote: Bright red berries on prickly green holly. It's starting to look a lot like Christmas!

44.description: Fieldfares in large flocks feeding on berries and in open fields
44.childFriendlyNote: Big chattering groups of fieldfares hop across fields. They flew here from the cold north!

44.description: Starling murmurations continuing through early winter, dramatic evening displays
44.childFriendlyNote: The starling sky-dance is still going! Wrap up warm and watch them paint shapes across the sunset!

45.description: Mistletoe clearly visible in bare tree canopies, white berries ripening in green leaf clusters
45.childFriendlyNote: Mistletoe hangs in the bare trees with white sticky berries. Mistle thrushes eat them and spread the seeds!

45.description: Tawny owls hooting through the long November nights, defending territories
45.childFriendlyNote: The dark evenings are filled with owl hoots. They're calling through the cold night air!

45.description: Robins singing their wistful autumn song from bare branches, defending winter feeding territories
45.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings a gentle, slightly sad song from a bare branch. It's guarding its winter garden!

45.description: Fieldfares in flocks across open fields and hedgerows, berry supplies dwindling
45.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares have eaten lots of berries already. They move to new hedges to find more!

45.description: Mistle thrushes singing boldly from treetops in wind and rain, guarding berry-laden trees
45.childFriendlyNote: This brave bird sings from the top of a tree even in the wildest wind and rain. People call it the storm cock!

46.description: Mistletoe prominent in bare tree canopies, white berries fully ripe, favoured by mistle thrushes
46.childFriendlyNote: Green mistletoe balls with white berries hang in the bare trees. Legend says you get a kiss underneath!

46.description: Mistle thrushes singing from exposed perches in rain and gale, their wild song defying the weather
46.childFriendlyNote: Rain and wind? The storm cock doesn't care. It sings louder than ever from the very top of the tree!

46.description: Tawny owls calling through long dark evenings, their hooting a familiar sound of winter
46.childFriendlyNote: "Hoo-hoo-hooooo" echoes through the dark. The owl is wide awake while you're snuggling in bed!

46.description: Robins visiting garden feeders, their orange-red breast bright in the grey November light
46.childFriendlyNote: The friendly robin hops close to you in the garden. It's hoping you'll turn up some tasty worms!

46.description: Holly berries still bright, some being stripped by hungry thrushes and blackbirds
46.childFriendlyNote: Red holly berries still glow in the hedges. Birds are eating them as fast as they can!

47.description: Mistle thrushes singing boldly from treetops, defending berry-laden trees through wind and rain
47.childFriendlyNote: The storm cock sings from the tallest tree in the wildest weather. What a brave bird!

47.description: Robins singing their wistful winter song, visiting feeders and following gardeners for worms
47.childFriendlyNote: The robin follows you around the garden hoping you'll dig up a worm. It's very cheeky!

47.description: Tawny owls calling through the darkness, pairs duetting in woodland and parks
47.childFriendlyNote: Two owls call to each other in the dark: "ke-wick!" says one, "hoo-hoo-hooo" replies the other!

47.description: Grey herons standing at canal edges and park ponds, patient hunters in the winter grey
47.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey bird stands like a statue by the canal. It can wait for ages without moving until a fish swims past!

47.description: First hard frosts transforming gardens and fields, ice crystals coating leaves, grass and spider webs
47.childFriendlyNote: Everything is white and sparkly! Frost has turned the grass into a crunchy crystal carpet. Breathe out and see your breath!

48.description: Robins puffed up against the cold, singing from bare branches and visiting garden feeders
48.childFriendlyNote: The robin puffs up into a fluffy ball to keep warm. It looks twice its size!

48.description: Mistle thrushes still singing from high perches, guarding berry trees fiercely
48.childFriendlyNote: The storm cock guards its berry tree like a tiny fierce dragon. It chases away any bird that comes near!

48.description: Grey herons hunched at water edges, patient and still in the cold late November air
48.childFriendlyNote: The grey heron stands perfectly still in the cold. It pulls its neck in to keep warm and waits for fish!

48.description: Holly berries still providing colour, glossy evergreen leaves bright against bare winter branches
48.childFriendlyNote: Prickly holly with red berries. It stays green all winter long while everything else goes bare!

48.description: Tawny owls calling in the early darkness of late November, long nights for hunting
48.childFriendlyNote: It gets dark so early now. The owl has extra hunting hours to find mice and voles!

49.description: Robins at garden feeders, bold and confiding, their red breast vivid against grey winter days
49.childFriendlyNote: The friendly robin is the bravest garden bird. It hops right up close to say hello!

49.description: Mistletoe with ripe white berries clearly visible in bare deciduous trees, traditional Christmas decoration
49.childFriendlyNote: Mistletoe with its white berries hangs in the bare trees. People have hung it indoors at Christmas for hundreds of years!

49.description: Holly berries and evergreen leaves providing vital colour, being collected for Christmas decorations
49.childFriendlyNote: Holly with its prickly leaves and red berries is the star of Christmas decorations!

49.description: Tawny owls hooting through December nights, beginning to establish breeding territories
49.childFriendlyNote: The owl calls through the frosty December night, "hoo-hoo-hooooo" echoes between the bare trees!

49.description: Grey herons at frozen pond edges and unfrozen canals, adapting to winter conditions
49.childFriendlyNote: The tall grey heron stands by the icy canal. When the pond freezes it moves to where water still flows!

50.description: Robins singing from bare branches and garden fences, defending winter territories
50.childFriendlyNote: Even in December the robin sings. Its cheerful tune brightens the shortest days of the year!

50.description: Mistletoe prominent in bare trees, collected for Christmas traditions across Western Europe
50.childFriendlyNote: Mistletoe balls hang in the bare winter trees. It's almost Christmas and time for mistletoe kisses!

50.description: Holly with red berries, a symbol of the season, birds feeding on remaining fruit
50.childFriendlyNote: Holly and its red berries, the perfect Christmas colours straight from nature!

50.description: Fieldfares in flocks feeding on remaining berries and in frozen fields
50.childFriendlyNote: Chattering fieldfares search for the last berries. They huddle together to keep warm!

50.description: Tawny owls calling in the long winter darkness, preparing for early breeding season
50.childFriendlyNote: The owl hoots through the longest nights of the year. It's already thinking about finding a mate!

51.description: Robins bold at garden feeders, their red breast the brightest colour in the grey December landscape
51.childFriendlyNote: The robin's orange-red chest glows like a tiny Christmas light in the grey winter garden!

51.description: Holly berries still bright, an essential food for winter thrushes and a Christmas symbol
51.childFriendlyNote: Bright red holly berries, the birds' Christmas dinner and our favourite decoration!

51.description: Magpies conspicuous in bare trees, iridescent black and white plumage gleaming in winter light
51.childFriendlyNote: The magpie's black feathers flash blue and green in the winter sun. It's like a walking rainbow!

51.description: Mistletoe with white berries in bare canopies, the Christmas tradition at its peak
51.childFriendlyNote: Mistletoe hangs in the bare trees with its waxy white berries, Merry Christmas!

51.description: Tawny owls calling through the longest nights, a familiar sound of the dark winter season
51.childFriendlyNote: On the longest night of the year the owl hoots and hoots. It doesn't mind the dark at all!

52.description: Robins singing from bare branches, one of the few birds still in full song during the darkest days
52.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings through the last days of the year. It never gives up, even in the coldest weather!

52.description: Christmas roses beginning to bloom again in sheltered spots, closing the year's cycle
52.childFriendlyNote: The Christmas rose is blooming again just in time. Nature's calendar has come all the way round!

52.description: Holly with remaining red berries, evergreen leaves providing shelter for roosting birds
52.childFriendlyNote: Holly stays green all year round. Little birds hide in its prickly leaves to keep safe and warm!

52.description: Fieldfares in winter flocks, feeding on the last hedgerow berries and in frosty fields
52.childFriendlyNote: The chattering fieldfares hop across frosty fields looking for food, what a tough life in winter!

52.description: Magpies visible in bare trees and on frosty lawns, their bold black and white pattern unmistakable
52.childFriendlyNote: The magpie struts across the frosty grass. It chatters and chatters like it's telling everyone the year-end news!
